block.statement: the ovk world is declared into existence
A communications professional at a PR company who prepares press releases and posts for clients and runs them through Before You Send before sending
block.name: pr-professional
priorities: know how content lands before it is public
evidence they can show a client

block.statement: When I have a press release or post ready to send for a client, I want to see how the intended audience would react to it, individually and as a group, so I can change it or retime it before it is public.
block.situation: I have a press release or post ready to send for a client
block.motivation: see how the intended audience would react to it, individually and as a group
block.outcome: change it or retime it before it is public

block.statement: Before You Send is used by PR companies: they run their press releases and posts through it before sending them
A piece of content is shown to each persona as an individual and to the personas as a group, and how they respond in each case is reported
Before You Send is not static: a persona's response depends on the state of the world when the content is tested, not on the content alone
The finding for a piece of content is the aggregate of persona responses across the population, one response per persona
Clients supply the past performance of their content as platform exports with per-post totals such as reach, reactions, comments and shares; work proceeds with the data as it is
Statistical sources named for building Tallinn personas are arvudes.tallinn.ee, strateegia.tallinn.ee and digiriik.eesti.ee
flow is the single event queue between everything: the simulation engine both reads from flow and writes to it, and every other consumer reads it through its own cursor
options_closed: components calling each other directly
batch jobs whose results live only in job folders

block.statement: Each persona is a constantly running process that consumes flow: it has its own stream of events that can influence its decisions, and it retains its own pool of knowledge
options_closed: personas created fresh for each test
personas with no memory between tests

block.statement: A persona that needs a model's judgement puts a request on flow as a job; multiple models, both LLMs and SLMs, pick up the job and respond, and their responses are aggregated into one response for that persona
options_closed: a single model answering for every persona
personas calling a model directly

block.statement: Prior posts and their real results are kept as a reality dataset, and the difference between what the system predicted and what happened is recorded in an errors table
options_closed: reporting simulated reactions with no check against real outcomes

block.statement: The new engine replaces the panels and personas of Before You Send; everything else in Before You Send stays the same
options_closed: rebuilding the Before You Send report or front end
keeping the existing panels and personas

block.statement: Personas are custom-built from statistical data about the real population they represent
options_closed: using MatrAIx's ready-made personas
hand-written personas

block.statement: Inputs other than the content are fed to personas and go into each persona's pool: relevant newspaper articles, time of day, weather reports, and levels of attitudes such as sexism and racism
options_closed: feeding personas the content alone

block.statement: How world inputs and attitude levels are represented for a persona is not yet designed: news articles, time of day, weather, and levels of sexism and racism, including whether such a level belongs to the persona, to the public climate, or to both
The rule for aggregating multiple model responses into one persona response is not decided
How the group response can be checked against reality is unclear while client exports hold comment counts but not comment text
A simulated panel's reactions to content predict how the real audience reacts better than simple rules such as post type or caption length do
block.impact: the report is opinion without evidence and the core claim of the product fails
block.validation_method: backtest on a client's past posts: rank posts by predicted reaction rate, compare with actual rates per person reached and with simple baselines, scored on a held-out recent period

block.statement: Feeding world inputs into persona pools brings reactions closer to reality than testing the content alone
block.impact: the constantly running loop per persona adds cost without adding accuracy
block.validation_method: replay the news and conditions for the dates of past posts and compare prediction error with and without them

block.statement: Aggregating the responses of multiple models gives a persona response closer to reality than one model's response
block.impact: every decision costs several model calls for no gain
block.validation_method: run the same backtest per model and for the aggregated response and compare errors

block.statement: Everything else improves a panel that must first be shown to predict a real audience at all; if it does not, no other part of the design matters
A PR professional submits content to be tested
block.story: As a PR professional I submit a press release or post so that the audience sees it before the public does
constraints: the rest of Before You Send is unchanged (AX-OVK-00013)

block.statement: A persona takes in a world input from its stream and it goes into its pool
block.story: As a persona I take in news and the time of day and the weather and the public climate so that my reactions reflect the world I am living in
constraints: inputs reach a persona only through flow (AX-OVK-00009)

block.statement: A persona that has received content puts a request on flow as a job
block.story: As a persona I ask for a judgement on the content in front of me so that I can respond to it
constraints: the request goes on flow and never directly to a model (AX-OVK-00011)

block.statement: Multiple models pick up the job and send back their responses
block.story: As a model I answer a persona's job so that the persona's response does not rest on one model alone
constraints: more than one model answers each job (AX-OVK-00011)

block.statement: The model responses to one job are aggregated into one response for that persona
block.story: As the aggregator I combine the model responses to a job so that each persona gives one response
constraints: exactly one response per persona per job (AX-OVK-00006)

block.statement: Persona responses are aggregated across the population into the result reported by Before You Send
block.story: As the aggregator I combine the persona responses so that the PR professional sees how the audience responded

block.statement: When the real result of a post is known the difference from the reported result is recorded in the errors table
block.story: As the aggregator I compare what was reported with what happened so that the system's accuracy is known
constraints: real results are the client exports as supplied (AX-OVK-00007)

block.statement: A test must not change the audience: a draft is shown to a temporary copy of each persona that is discarded afterwards, and only content a client really publishes enters persona memory
options_closed: personas remembering drafts they were tested on

block.statement: One client's unpublished draft must never reach a panel that another client tests against
Each report records the point in the flow log it ran against, so that it can be rerun exactly
options_closed: reports that cannot be reproduced

block.statement: A constantly running persona is idle until an event arrives on its stream; small models make the cheap decision of whether the persona notices it, and larger models are used for reactions to drafts
options_closed: personas computing on a clock
a large model call for every event

block.statement: Every persona answer is checked for character breaks before it reaches a report: the wrong language, details that contradict the persona's identity, and facts that contradict the content
options_closed: showing unchecked model answers to a client

block.statement: The most recent quarter of a client's data is held back for testing and never used for tuning, and posts published after the models' training cutoffs are preferred for testing
options_closed: tuning and testing on the same posts

block.statement: Model responses to a job are aggregated as structured reactions, and the persona's comment is one real model comment quoted word for word in place of blended text
block.supersession_reason: The owner accepted the recommended aggregation rule, which resolves this unknown
options_closed: another model rewriting several answers into one

block.statement: Not all data holds the same weight, not all clients have the same data, and not all social media platforms hold the same weight
The same data is required from every client in order to onboard them
The data request to a client is made by someone upstream of this team, so it must be simple enough to pass along unexplained
The onboarding standard is the data present in the sample export: we work only with data we can actually get, and accept the capabilities this removes
options_closed: asking clients for data beyond the standard export
designing around data clients cannot supply

block.statement: Text comes before video: posts are tested on their text now, photo posts are included and tested on their caption, and video is looked at later
options_closed: video analysis in the first phase
excluding photo posts

block.statement: Facebook is prioritised, with Instagram second
options_closed: starting with TikTok or YouTube
treating all platforms as equal

block.statement: The request to a client is one instruction: a post-level export from Meta Business Suite for the Facebook page and Instagram account covering the last 12 months
options_closed: a custom data request per client

block.statement: Must-have onboarding data for every post: post text, publish date and time, post type, reach, reactions or likes, comment count, share count, and post ID or link
options_closed: onboarding a client whose data lacks any of these

block.statement: Should-have onboarding data, used where present and never a condition of onboarding: organic versus paid reach, hides, and clicks; in the sample these exist for Facebook and not for Instagram
options_closed: making these a condition of onboarding

block.statement: Could-have onboarding data, used if present: views, and Instagram saves and follows
options_closed: making these a condition of onboarding

block.statement: Won't-have for now: comment text, reaction types, image files and follower demographics because they are not in the sample; video metrics, viewer age and gender, country breakdown, and TikTok and YouTube data because video is a later phase
options_closed: requesting these from clients in this phase

block.statement: Outcomes are measured per person reached and not as totals, because reach is set by the platform and by paid promotion
The Before You Send report is built from persona responses and not from client data, so under these constraints it is still produced in full; client data is used to check it

With the standard data these parts of the report can be checked against reality: would-post-publicly against comment and share rates, and strength of reaction against engagement per person reached; worth-a-second-look can be partly checked against clicks, on Facebook only
With the standard data sentiment and backlash risk can be checked only weakly: hides are the only negative signal, they exist on Facebook only, and reactions are not split by type

With the standard data these parts of the report cannot be checked against reality: reaction themes, each persona's private reaction, where a persona stopped reading, attention words, the acceptability heatmap, the wording of public comments, and reach
Under the onboarding standard the group response can be built and shown but cannot be scored against reality, because comment text is not collected
A panel percentage is not a forecast of a real rate; the claim the data supports is a comparison of a draft with the client's own past posts
In the Meta export the column names are in the client's language and the post text sits in either the title column or the description column, so both are read and each language needs a column mapping
Whether other clients can supply the same export as the sample is unverified: only one client's export has been seen
Whether a panel built from population statistics matches a client's actual followers cannot be confirmed, because follower demographics are not in the onboarding standard
The minimum number of posts a client needs for the backtest to mean anything is not established
Whether clients are told which parts of the report are checked against reality and which are illustrative is undecided
How the structured parts of several model responses are combined is not chosen: by vote and middle value, or by a recorded random pick
Whether Facebook should come first for every client is unverified: the priority rests on one client, a political party, and a different kind of client may have its audience elsewhere
Reaction, comment and share rates per person reached are an adequate measure of how a post landed with its audience
block.impact: the reality dataset measures the wrong thing and a panel tuned to it is tuned to platform behaviour instead of audience reaction
block.validation_method: where a client can supply comment text or survey results, compare them with the engagement rates for the same posts

block.statement: Hides are a usable signal of negative reaction for checking backlash risk
block.impact: backlash risk, the section clients care about most, has no check against reality
block.validation_method: test whether posts the panel rates as high backlash risk have higher hide rates, on the held-back quarter

block.statement: A caption can be tested on its own for photo posts, without the image
block.impact: predictions for photo posts, the majority of text-bearing posts, are unreliable
block.validation_method: compare backtest error on photo posts with error on text and link posts

block.statement: Clients put two kinds of content through Before You Send: social posts, which the public reads directly, and press releases, which are written for journalists
A press release reaches the public second-hand: a journalist or editor reads it first and decides whether and how to cover it, and the public reads the resulting coverage
The design, the sample data and the onboarding standard so far cover social posts only; press releases are not yet covered
How a press release is tested is not designed: with a panel of journalists, with simulated coverage shown to the public panel, or both
What the reality data for press releases is, and whether clients can supply it, is unknown: media monitoring of coverage is the likely source and it is not in the sample
Which other channels matter has not been assessed: news site comment sections, email newsletters, LinkedIn and X have been named
PR works in two hops: the agency sends to the media, the media produce coverage, and the public reads the coverage; it is not a direct-to-consumer path
Journalists are a panel, built as personas like any other; they are types, such as a business reporter at a national daily, and never simulations of named real journalists
options_closed: simulating named real journalists
testing press releases on the public panel alone

block.statement: Coverage produced by the journalist panel goes onto flow and enters the public personas' streams as news
options_closed: treating the public's reaction to the release text as a prediction of public response

block.statement: What the report shows for a press release is not designed: likelihood of pickup, probable headlines by outlet and the hard questions have been named, and this needs AX-OVK-00013, which keeps everything else in Before You Send the same, to be revisited
A press release is tested in two hops: the journalist panel decides whether and how to cover it (AX-OVK-00072), and the coverage is then read by the public panel (AX-OVK-00073)
block.supersession_reason: The owner decided on a journalist panel whose coverage feeds the public panel, which answers this unknown
context_shift: PR was recognised as agency to media to public and not direct to consumer
options_closed: choosing only one of the two hops

block.statement: We look at this through the eyes and lens of the person who is releasing the content in order to communicate
The organisation whose message it is and whose reputation is at stake, such as a city government or a political party; a client of the PR agency
block.name: agency-client
priorities: the public understands or acts as intended

block.statement: The person releasing the content is both the PR professional at the agency, who writes and sends it, and the agency's client, whose message it is; the lens of AX-OVK-00076 is both, and the two can want different things

What the sender is trying to achieve is an input alongside the content: what they want people to understand, feel or do, and who it is aimed at; the report judges whether the content arrived as intended
options_closed: taking the content as the only input
reporting reactions without reference to what the sender intended

block.statement: How the sender's intent is captured and how the report judges against it is not designed; where the two senders want different things it is unclear whose intent is used; and adding this input needs AX-OVK-00013, which keeps everything else in Before You Send the same, to be revisited
We look at this from the lens of the person being communicated to
What the report measures is the gap between what the sender intends and what the receiver takes away
The person being communicated to is both the journalist, who receives the release, and the member of the public, who reads the coverage or the post; the lens of AX-OVK-00081 is both
The new engine replaces the panels and personas of Before You Send; for now the existing report is kept and added to, not redesigned
block.supersession_reason: Later decisions need things the current report does not have: a report for press releases, the sender's intent as an input, and the gap between intent and reception. The owner chose to add to the report for now
context_shift: press releases need their own report content
the sender's intent became an input
the report measures the gap between intent and reception
options_closed: keeping the existing panels and personas
redesigning the report around the two lenses for now

block.statement: The engine's boundary is the flow queue: content arrives from the agency on flow and results are returned to flow for the agency; the engine returns its data and does not decide what is shown
options_closed: the engine producing the report itself
holding back data because nothing uses it yet

block.statement: Separation of labour: what is used from the returned data, and how it is presented, is worked out after it is on the queue, by a customer advocate working from the customer's side

These open questions belong to the customer advocate's side and not to the engine: what the report shows for a press release (AX-OVK-00074), whether clients are told which parts of the report are checked (AX-OVK-00059), and how the report judges against the sender's intent (part of AX-OVK-00080); how intent is captured as an input stays with the engine
A post is client specific: content submitted for testing is a job for that client, and the result is the response to that job
Safeguards that keep each client's jobs and responses separate are put in as the work proceeds
options_closed: designing every safeguard before building anything

block.statement: The response to a job is the contract between the engine and whatever presents it: it returns everything the engine produced, in structured form, with each item marked as needed now or as extra
options_closed: returning only what the current report uses

block.statement: A response is made up of events on flow that all carry the job ID: one for each persona's response and one for the panel as a whole

Every response carries an envelope: the job ID, the client, the content exactly as tested, the content type, the sender's intent as given, the panel and its composition, the models used, the log position the run used, the time, the version of the response contract, and whether the run completed in full with what failed if it did not
options_closed: a response that cannot be traced to its job and its inputs

block.statement: Needed now, for each persona: age, gender, district and language; the private reaction in their words; where they stopped reading; the words that caught their attention; how they felt about each sentence; what they would say publicly and whether they would post it; an anxiety score and a negative-to-positive score; and openness, agreeableness and worry
options_closed: dropping anything the current report draws

block.statement: Needed now, across the panel: positive, neutral and negative counts; the share who would post publicly; the share worth a second look; and reaction themes with counts
options_closed: dropping anything the current report draws

block.statement: Extra, for each persona, from the two lenses: the takeaway in one sentence; what they would do next; the questions they are left with; what was unclear or not in their language; whether it was relevant or useful to them; how they would retell it to someone else; and what they now think of the sender
options_closed: returning only reactions

block.statement: Extra, across the panel, from the start: the trait that best explains where the audience splits; the loud minority, who feel strongly and would post; the silent unhappy, who react badly and would say nothing; and the distance between what each persona thought and what they would say
options_closed: returning only counts and averages

block.statement: About the result itself, on every response: each model's answer and the merged answer for each persona; how far the models agreed; the outcome of the character check; each persona's answer alone and in the group; and for every item its confidence and whether it can be checked against reality
options_closed: returning a finding without its confidence
returning only the merged answer

block.statement: Returned once the reality dataset exists: the client's most similar past posts and how they did; what a simple rule would have predicted; how the draft compares with the client's history; and later, matched by job ID, the real result and the error
options_closed: leaving the reality dataset out of the response

block.statement: Returned once the sender's intent is an input: the gap between the intent and each takeaway; the sender's key point set against where people stopped reading; who was aimed at and did not notice or stopped early; and who reacted without being aimed at
options_closed: reporting reactions without the gap to intent

block.statement: Returned as the larger parts are built: from the journalist panel whether they would cover it and why, the headline and angle, what they would cut and add, the questions they would put to the sender, and the draft coverage; the gap at each hop and which of the sender's points survive; what in a persona's recent experience shaped its reaction; what the content collides with in the news and how it would land on another day; whether it repeats or contradicts the client's earlier messages; which sentence does the damage when removed; who changed their mind in the group; and whether a rerun gives the same finding
options_closed: treating the first version of the response as complete

block.statement: A persona's private reaction and stop point are taken before any further question is put to it
options_closed: asking the extra questions first

block.statement: The list of what is needed now and the stages in which the rest is returned are expected to change
Items in a response are plausible and not proven: a split found in a small panel can be noise, and a persona reporting on itself is the weakest kind of evidence
The exact structure and field names of the response are not designed
How confidence is calculated for each item in a response is not designed
How the engine learns that a tested draft was published, and in which version, is not designed; it is needed to match a real result to its job and to let published content enter persona memory
How many extra questions can be put to a persona before they change its answers or cost too much is not known
What a persona reports about itself, such as its takeaway, its next action and how it would retell the content, is informative about real receivers
block.impact: the extra items in the response describe the models and not the audience
block.validation_method: compare the share of personas whose next action is to comment or share with the real comment and share rates for the same posts

block.statement: The engine operates on the basis that, given what it is supplied, it does what it can and sends back what is interesting; whether any of it is used in a UI is for others to choose
A response states which inputs it was given, what it could therefore produce, and what it could not produce and why; a missing input reduces the response and never fails the job
options_closed: failing a job because an optional input is missing
a response that hides what it could not do

block.statement: The same export is requested again each quarter; published posts are matched to their jobs by their text; and where the published text differs from the tested draft, the published text is run through the engine and that is what is scored
options_closed: relying on the agency to report what was published
scoring a prediction that was made for different wording

block.statement: The engine learns that a tested draft was published, and in which version, from the quarterly export, by matching published posts to their jobs by text (AX-OVK-00111); this covers social posts and not press releases
block.supersession_reason: The owner decided to request the same export each quarter, which shows what was published without the agency reporting it
context_shift: a repeat of the onboarding export each quarter was decided
options_closed: relying on the agency to report what was published

block.statement: How close the wording of a published post must be to a tested draft to count as the same post is not defined, nor what happens when a draft was rewritten so heavily that no match is found
